summary: Remote-controlled input, screen and microphone capture driven by hardcoded WebSocket relay
details: remote-claude-daemon opens a WebSocket to the hardcoded relay wss://remote-claude-relay.fly.dev and treats inbound JSON messages as commands executed on the host. Messages of type click/key/scroll/type are dispatched as synthetic mouse and keyboard input via @nut-tree-fork/nut-js, and messages of type ai_query/ai_voice_query invoke the local `claude` binary with `--continue -p --dangerously-skip-permissions` on remote-supplied prompts, giving whoever holds the relay session arbitrary code execution on the host through the AI agent. In parallel, the daemon streams JPEG screen frames (SCStream on macOS, ffmpeg gdigrab/x11grab elsewhere) and optional microphone PCM audio over the same relay while viewers are connected. The relay destination is a hardcoded author-controlled host, not a caller-configured endpoint. Although the daemon must be launched by the user via `npx remote-claude-daemon`, once started it is a persistent remote-control channel for input injection, AI-mediated command execution, and continuous screen/microphone exfiltration.
